Sustain an injury during a hazardous athletic event.
Substitute a temporary replacement for an official.
Subject a material to intense laboratory testing.

mnemonics: Substantiate contains substance, meaning you need substance or proof to back it up.

senses.definition: Serving no useful purpose; having no excuse for being.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Unnecessary and completely useless.

examples.text: The long preamble felt entirely superfluous given the urgent nature of the agenda.
Removing the superfluous details made the final report much easier to read.
She packed several superfluous outfits that she never wore during the entire journey.
Any further explanation would be superfluous and waste the committee members time.

distractors.lemma: Flowing smoothly over a surface without any resistance.
Supervising a complex project with extreme care.
Superior in quality to all competing products.
Spanning a vast distance across open water.
Surpassing previous records in athletic competition.

senses.definition: More than is needed, desired, or required.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Having more than enough of something.

examples.text: They donated the superfluous harvest to the local community kitchen.
The manuscript contained superfluous chapters that the editor wisely decided to trim.
Bringing a heavy winter coat to the tropical island proved superfluous.
The generous endowment left the library with superfluous funds for new acquisitions.
Delete superfluous (or unnecessary) words

distractors.lemma: Superior in strength and agility compared to rivals.
Superficial in appearance without any deep foundation.
Supplied with necessary provisions for a long voyage.
Supremacy achieved through political dominance.
Subordinate to a higher governing authority.

mnemonics: Super-flu means extra fluid that overflows and is completely useless.

senses.definition: The state of being more than full.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: An excessive amount that leaves you completely stuffed.

examples.text: After the grand banquet, guests suffered from a surfeit of rich pastries.
The library faced a surfeit of donated books with nowhere to store them.
A surfeit of information often leads to confusion rather than clarity.
He experienced a surfeit of praise that eventually made him quite uncomfortable.

distractors.lemma: Surface tension that prevents liquid from spilling.
Surplus revenue generated by a successful enterprise.
A sudden drop in temperature during autumn.
Suffering caused by prolonged physical labor.
Surveillance conducted by local security forces.

senses.definition: The quality of being so overabundant that prices fall.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: An oversupply so massive that the market value crashes.

examples.text: A sudden surfeit of imported grain caused local farmers to lower their prices drastically.
The agricultural market crashed due to a seasonal surfeit of dairy products.
Economists warned that a surfeit of crude oil would destabilize regional markets.
Retailers panicked over a surfeit of winter coats remaining unsold by spring.

distractors.lemma: A surface defect caused by improper manufacturing.
Surging inflation that erodes purchasing power.
A sudden freeze that destroys agricultural yields.
Substantial debt accumulated over multiple fiscal years.
Superior credit ratings issued by financial agencies.

senses.definition: Eating until excessively full.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: The act of eating or drinking way too much.

examples.text: His stomach ached after a long evening of festive surfeit.
Medieval feasts often resulted in severe illness caused by sheer surfeit.
The physician blamed his patient's ailments on a chronic surfeit of heavy foods.
Moderation in diet helps prevent the discomforts of sudden surfeit.

distractors.lemma: Surrendering to fatigue during a strenuous hike.
Supporting a heavy weight with structural beams.
Suppressing an appetite through medication.
Surpassing nutritional standards recommended by experts.
Succeeding in a competitive eating contest.

mnemonics: Surf and eat until you have a surfeit.

senses.definition: Marked by quiet and caution and secrecy; taking pains to avoid being observed.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Done in a very sneaky and quiet way to avoid notice.

examples.text: She cast a surreptitious glance at the answer key while the proctor was looking away.
The spies exchanged surreptitious whispers in the crowded railway station.
He made a surreptitious exit from the boring gala through the garden doors.
The detective conducted a surreptitious investigation into the missing funds.
A surreptitious glance at his watch

distractors.lemma: Surrounded by armed guards in a high security facility.
Supporting a controversial cause with public demonstrations.
Supervising workers with strict attention to detail.
Sustaining severe damage from a violent storm.
Supplementing income through part-time employment.

senses.definition: Conducted with or marked by hidden aims or methods.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Carried out with hidden motives or a secret agenda.

examples.text: The board members grew suspicious of his surreptitious attempts to alter the company charter.
Their surreptitious negotiations took place behind closed doors late at night.
The government launched a surreptitious operation to monitor suspected dissidents.
Behind the polite smiles lay a surreptitious plan to seize control of the enterprise.
Surreptitious mobilization of troops

distractors.lemma: Structured carefully to meet rigorous academic standards.
Subordinated to the primary goals of the organization.
Substituted with alternative materials of lower quality.
Superficial in design without any underlying purpose.
Supplied with adequate resources for the mission.

mnemonics: Reptiles move silently and stealthily, much like something surreptitious.

senses.definition: A person who tries to please someone in order to gain a personal advantage.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: A person who acts overly nice to important people just to get ahead.

examples.text: The ambitious manager became a notorious sycophant whenever the regional director visited the office.
Surrounded by a court of obedient advisers, the monarch could no longer distinguish a genuine friend from a mere sycophant.
She despised the corporate ladder climbers who used flattery like a sycophant to secure promotions.
Instead of offering honest feedback, the timid employee acted like a sycophant during every meeting.

distractors.lemma: An instrument used for measuring the intensity of light or sound waves.
A medical specialist who treats disorders of the central nervous system.
A botanical specimen characterized by thick fleshy leaves and bright blossoms.
A malicious spirit believed to cause misfortune in ancient folklore.
A device designed to purify contaminated water through distillation.

mnemonics: A sick elephant will do anything to please its keeper for extra peanuts.

senses.definition: Habitually reserved and uncommunicative.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Someone who is quiet and does not talk very much.

examples.text: Known for his quiet demeanor, the taciturn detective rarely offered more than a single nod in response.
The old lighthouse keeper remained taciturn throughout the long winter evening.
Her usually taciturn brother surprised the family by delivering a lengthy toast.
Diplomats must remain cautious and taciturn during tense international negotiations.

distractors.lemma: Excessively loud and talkative in social gatherings.
Characterized by rapid changes in mood and temperament.
Prone to sudden bursts of aggressive behavior.
Showing extreme dedication to a particular cause.
Marked by sophisticated charm and elegance.

mnemonics: Think of tac-i-turn as turning away from talking.

senses.definition: Of superficial relevance if any.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Something that is only slightly related to the main topic.

examples.text: The professor indulged in a lengthy anecdote that remained entirely tangential to the lecture.
We must avoid getting bogged down in tangential details if we want to finish the project on time.
His remarks about local weather patterns were merely tangential to the economic summit.
She raised several interesting points, though most of them were tangential to our core argument.
A tangential remark

distractors.lemma: Forming a straight line between two distinct points.
Possessing immense physical strength and durability.
Related directly to the primary objective of a study.
Requiring immediate attention due to extreme urgency.
Existing in a physical state between solid and liquid.

senses.definition: Of or relating to or acting along or in the direction of a tangent.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Moving along the edge of a curve or touching a surface at only one point.

examples.text: The geometry student calculated the vector of the tangential force applied to the wheel.
A straight line drawn perpendicular to the radius forms a tangential path along the circle.
The spacecraft maintained a tangential trajectory as it skimmed the upper atmosphere.
Engineers analyzed the tangential stress exerted on the rotating turbine blades.
Tangential forces

distractors.lemma: Moving directly toward the exact center of a mass.
Spreading evenly across a three dimensional volume.
Intersecting two parallel lines at an acute angle.
Exhibiting circular motion around a fixed pivot point.
Extending outward from the core in opposite directions.

mnemonics: A tangent line just touches a curve at one point, barely related.

senses.definition: Having thin consistency.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Having a very thin or watery texture.

examples.text: The soup was ruined by its watery and tenuous consistency.
Chemists noted the tenuous nature of the newly formed gel before it hardened.
The sauce retained a tenuous quality despite hours of simmering.
He tested the tenuous fluid to see if it would pass through the fine filter.
A tenuous fluid

Hardened into a solid crystal structure under pressure.
Composed of heavy metal particles suspended in oil.
Displaying bright iridescent colors when exposed to light.
Absorbing moisture rapidly from the surrounding air.

senses.definition: Very thin in gauge or diameter.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Extremely thin in width or diameter.

examples.text: The jeweler worked with tenuous strands of gold wire to create the delicate filigree.
Spider silk is renowned for being exceptionally strong despite its tenuous fibers.
The artisan wove the fabric using tenuous threads of raw silk.
Microscopic cracks appeared along the tenuous beams of the suspension bridge.
A tenuous thread

distractors.lemma: Built with heavy and robust structural timbers.
Wide and expansive in overall surface area.
Shaped into a flat rectangular block of metal.
Coated with a thick layer of protective enamel.
Consisting of multiple braided ropes of hemp.

senses.definition: Lacking substance or significance.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Very weak, flimsy, or lacking any real importance.

There is only a tenuous link between the two historical events.
Her hope of winning the championship rested on a tenuous thread.
A tenuous argument

distractors.lemma: Supported by overwhelming empirical evidence and facts.
Of monumental historical significance and influence.
Extremely rigid and resistant to any form of change.
Completely false and fabricated by malicious actors.
Deeply rooted in ancient traditions and customs.

mnemonics: Tenuous sounds like thin tissue paper.

senses.definition: Brief and to the point; effectively cut short.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Short and direct, using very few words.

Her prose style is remarkably terse, conveying complex emotions with minimal vocabulary.
The general sent a terse message confirming the victory.
Short and terse and easy to understand

distractors.lemma: Wordy and rambling in explanation.
Filled with elaborate metaphors and poetic imagery.
Polite and overly gracious in tone.
Hesitant and uncertain in delivery.
Filled with emotional outbursts and complaints.

senses.definition: Timid by nature or revealing timidity.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Easily frightened or lacking in courage.

examples.text: The timorous kitten hid beneath the heavy velvet sofa during the thunderstorm.
Her timorous voice barely carried across the quiet lecture hall.
He offered a timorous defense of his unconventional policy proposals.
A timorous approach to the market might cause the firm to miss profitable opportunities.
Timorous little mouse
In a timorous tone

distractors.lemma: Temperate in judgment and balanced in execution.
Characterized by loud demands and aggressive behavior.
Filled with malicious intent toward others.
Marked by excessive decoration and elaborate detail.

senses.definition: Slow and apathetic.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Lacking energy and moving very slowly.

After a heavy midday meal, his mind remained torpid for hours.

Visitors often found the museum staff delightfully relaxed yet slightly torpid.
A mind grown torpid in old age

distractors.lemma: Rapid and unpredictable in movement.
Extremely sharp and perceptive in analysis.
Related to the generation of heat.
Rigidly structured and inflexible in design.

senses.definition: In a condition of biological rest or suspended animation.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: In a state of dormancy or biological hibernation.

Bears enter a torpid condition that conserves energy during freezing weather.
Researchers monitored the torpid creatures in their natural habitat.
Torpid frogs

Covered in thick protective scales.
Capable of rapid flight over long distances.
Found exclusively in deep oceanic trenches.

Tortuous negotiations lasting for months

distractors.lemma: Pertaining to the science of baking pastry.
Painful and agonizing to physical endurance.
Extremely brief and lacking necessary detail.
Accurate and precise in mathematical calculation.

senses.definition: Marked by repeated turns and bends.

distractors.lemma: Completely flat and devoid of vegetation.

Underground and hidden from daylight.

senses.definition: Not straightforward.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Indirect or deceitful in method.

Avoid using tortuous tactics when a direct conversation will suffice.

distractors.lemma: Honest and transparent in all dealings.
Aggressive and confrontational in style.
Pertaining to formal legal proceedings.
Generous and charitable toward the needy.

senses.definition: Easily managed (controlled or taught or molded).

Capable of producing loud acoustic resonance.

senses.definition: Responsive to suggestions and influences.

distractors.lemma: Stubbornly resistant to any form of persuasion.

senses.definition: Having keenness and forcefulness and penetration in thought, expression, or intellect.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Having sharp, clever, and powerful insight in your thinking or speech.

Trenchant criticism

Marked by quiet hesitation and extreme reluctance to speak.
Existing in a physical state of decay and rot.
Exhibiting a tendency to wander aimlessly from topic to topic.

senses.definition: Characterized by or full of force and vigor.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Full of strong energy, power, and enthusiasm.

examples.text: The leader pursued reform with a trenchant determination that surprised everyone.

She approached every challenge with a trenchant spirit of ambition.

distractors.lemma: Lacking physical strength or emotional endurance.
Moving with deliberate and sluggish slowness.
Subject to sudden and unpredictable emotional shifts.
Showing deep sadness and sorrow over a loss.

senses.definition: Clearly or sharply defined to the mind.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Clear and distinct in your mind.

examples.text: The historian retained a trenchant memory of the turbulent era.
Her goals for the future remained trenchant despite the uncertainty.
He offered a trenchant outline of the proposed architecture.
The instructions were so trenchant that no one made a mistake.

distractors.lemma: Obscure and difficult to comprehend without specialized training.
Blurry and lacking any discernible visual structure.
Existing only in the realm of abstract theory.
Concealed intentionally from public view.

mnemonics: Think of trenchant as cutting a trench through confusion with sharp thoughts.

senses.definition: Defiantly aggressive.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Aggressive, hostile, and always ready to fight or argue.

He became truculent when the referee questioned his foul.

She faced the hostile committee with a truculent attitude.
A truculent speech against the new government

distractors.lemma: Written with extreme brevity and concise elegance.

senses.definition: Abnormally distended especially by fluids or gas.

The river became turgid after days of heavy rainfall.
Overwatering left the leaves of the houseplant looking turgid and heavy.

Smooth and polished to a reflective shine.

Fragmented into tiny, microscopic particles.

senses.definition: A corrupt or depraved or degenerate act or practice.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: A wicked, corrupt, or deeply immoral action.

History judges dictators harshly for their institutional turpitude.
The novel explores themes of greed and moral turpitude in high society.
Such acts of turpitude have no place in a civil society.

distractors.lemma: A sudden surge of overwhelming gratitude.
An attitude of extreme caution and careful planning.
A formal ceremony celebrating a historical milestone.
The quality of possessing great physical endurance.

distractors.lemma: Rarely seen and difficult to locate in the wild.

Moving at a speed faster than the human eye can track.
Hidden underground away from public view.

senses.definition: A feeling of anger caused by being offended.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Getting upset or annoyed because someone insulted or slighted you.

There was no need to take umbrage at such a mild remark.

distractors.lemma: A heavy shade cast by trees during the peak of noon.
An unexpected monetary bonus given for exceptional performance.
A sudden rush of wind blowing from the mountain range.
The architectural support beneath a stone bridge.

senses.definition: Unpleasantly and excessively suave or ingratiating in manner or speech.

distractors.lemma: Covered in a thick layer of natural oil or grease.

Marked by unusual brightness and clarity of expression.

mnemonics: Unctuous sounds like ointment, which is greasy and slick, just like an unctuous person's personality.

The distant mountains undulate against the pale sky.

distractors.lemma: To stand completely rigid without any movement.

To expand outward in a perfectly flat plane.
To sink slowly into the underlying earth.

senses.definition: Express criticism towards.

senses.definition: Showing a high degree of refinement and the assurance that comes from wide social experience.

Marked by extreme poverty and lack of resources.
Showing intense passion and emotional volatility.

distractors.lemma: Displaying excessive emotional sensitivity toward minor issues.

senses.definition: Cause annoyance in; disturb, especially by minor irritations.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: To irritate or annoy someone over small matters.

examples.text: The constant dripping of the leaky faucet began to vex the residents.
Minor inconveniences can quickly vex an impatient traveler.
Do not let trivial complaints vex your peaceful disposition.
The buzzing insect continued to vex him while he worked.

distractors.lemma: To cause physical injury through rough handling.
To puzzle someone with a complex mathematical riddle.
To frighten an animal by making sudden loud noises.
To please someone with unexpected gifts.

senses.definition: Disturb the peace of mind of; afflict with mental agitation or distress.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: To cause mental distress or anxiety.

examples.text: Difficult financial choices began to vex her troubled mind.
The mysterious disappearance continued to vex local authorities.
Unresolved family conflicts can deeply vex a sensitive soul.
The complex ethical dilemma served to vex the committee members.

distractors.lemma: To soothe someone into a peaceful and deep sleep.
To exhaust physical strength through heavy manual labor.
To cure a lingering illness with bitter medicine.
To clarify a confusing situation with clear evidence.

senses.definition: Change the arrangement or position of.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: To change the arrangement or position of something.

examples.text: The curator had to vex the ancient manuscript in the display case to prevent light damage.
She gently began to vex the decorative stones until the mosaic pattern looked balanced.
Workers used specialized tools to vex the heavy steel beams into proper alignment.

distractors.lemma: Cause annoyance or distress to a person.
Express extreme anger or frustration verbally.
Examine closely for hidden defects.
Conceal from view under a layer of material.

mnemonics: Vex rhymes with Rex, a dog that irritates the cat.

senses.definition: Spread negative information about.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: To spread negative information about someone.

examples.text: Unscrupulous politicians often try to vilify their opponents during a tight election campaign.
The tabloid newspapers sought to vilify the innocent celebrity with fabricated stories.
History tends to vilify leaders who betray public trust for personal gain.
It is unfair to vilify an entire organization based on the actions of one member.
The Nazi propaganda vilified the Jews

distractors.lemma: Glorify someone through exaggerated praise.
Verify facts before publishing a report.
Clarify a complex legal document.
Purify water using chemical filters.

mnemonics: Think of a vile person who likes to fly around spreading nasty rumors.

senses.definition: Show to be right by providing justification or proof.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: To show something is right by providing justification or proof.

examples.text: New forensic evidence would soon vindicate the suspect who had spent years in prison.
The scientist hoped her experimental results would vindicate the controversial theory.
Subsequent market trends helped to vindicate the cautious strategy of the investors.
His decision to resign will likely vindicate those who questioned his leadership.
Vindicate a claim

distractors.lemma: Violate an established rule or regulation.
Ventilate a room to improve air quality.
Indicate a preference for a specific outcome.
Fabricate evidence to secure a conviction.

senses.definition: Maintain, uphold, or defend.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: To maintain, uphold, or defend a principle or cause.

examples.text: The organization exists to vindicate the civil rights of marginalized citizens.
Brave journalists will always strive to vindicate freedom of the press.
Citizens gathered in the town square to vindicate the traditional liberties of the community.
Vindicate the rights of the citizens

distractors.lemma: Abandon a cherished belief under pressure.
Complicate a simple legal proceeding.
Liquidate assets to pay off mounting debts.
Obliterate records of past transactions.

senses.definition: Clear of accusation, blame, suspicion, or doubt with supporting proof.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: To clear someone of accusation, blame, suspicion, or doubt with supporting proof.

examples.text: DNA testing ultimately served to vindicate the wrongfully accused man.
The audit report completely cleared and helped to vindicate the director of any financial wrongdoing.
Witness testimony helped to vindicate her when her honesty was called into question.
You must vindicate yourself and fight this libel

distractors.lemma: Inculpate an innocent party in a crime.
Indict a suspect without sufficient evidence.
Vandalize public property during a protest.
Validate a parking ticket at the exit.

mnemonics: Vindicate sounds like win dictate, meaning your proof wins the argument.

senses.definition: Extremely poisonous or injurious; producing venom.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Extremely poisonous or injurious, producing venom.

examples.text: The jungle explorer wore heavy leather boots to protect against virulent snakes.
Certain exotic dart frogs secrete a virulent toxin through their brightly colored skin.
Antivenom is required immediately after a bite from such a virulent creature.
A virulent insect bite

distractors.lemma: Virtual in nature and lacking physical form.
Virtuous and adhering to strict moral standards.
Vigilant in watching out for potential dangers.
Volatile and prone to rapid evaporation.

senses.definition: Infectious; having the ability to cause disease.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Infectious and having the ability to cause severe disease.

examples.text: Public health officials tracked the spread of a virulent strain of influenza across the continent.
The pathogen proved unusually virulent, overwhelming patients within a matter of days.
Quarantine protocols were established to contain the virulent outbreak in the city.

distractors.lemma: Benign and completely harmless to human health.
Dormant and showing no active symptoms.
Nutritious and supportive of immune function.
Bactericidal and capable of destroying germs.

senses.definition: Harsh or corrosive in tone.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Harsh or corrosive in tone, often expressing intense hostility.

examples.text: The two rival politicians exchanged virulent insults during the televised debate.
She faced a virulent backlash on social media after expressing her controversial opinion.
The editorial was filled with virulent criticism of the administration's economic policies.

distractors.lemma: Complimentary and full of polite praise.
Ambiguous and open to multiple interpretations.
Apathetic and showing a lack of emotion.
Melancholic and expressive of profound sadness.

mnemonics: Virulent contains virus, reminding you of something harmful and toxic.

senses.definition: Having a relatively high resistance to flow.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Thick and slow moving like honey or syrup.

examples.text: The thick oil was so viscous that it poured out of the bottle in a single sluggish stream.
Cold molasses is far more viscous than water and takes several minutes to empty from a pitcher.
Engineers added a special polymer to make the lubricating fluid more viscous under high heat.
Lava from certain volcanoes is extremely viscous and crawls slowly down the mountain slopes.

distractors.lemma: Possessing a bright and luminous quality that reflects light.
Marked by extreme sharpness and clarity of form.
Displaying a tendency to shatter upon impact.
Exhibiting a faded or washed out appearance.
Moving with incredible speed and velocity.

senses.definition: Having the sticky properties of an adhesive.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Sticky and glue like to the touch.

examples.text: The sap leaking from the pine tree left a viscous residue on my fingers.
Children often leave viscous fingerprints on glass surfaces after eating candy.
The envelope flap was sealed with a viscous substance that required only a brief press.
A viscous coating on the stem of the plant traps small insects.

distractors.lemma: Tending to slip away easily from grasp.
Having a completely dry and powdery texture.
Lacking any form of physical substance.
Resistant to moisture and external decay.
Possessing a smooth and polished surface.

mnemonics: Think of viscous as viscous soup that flows as slow as us.

senses.definition: Spread negative information about.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: To yell at someone and say harsh things about them.

examples.text: The disgruntled critic began to vituperate the young author in a scathing online review.
It is unwise to vituperate your colleagues in public settings.
Politicians often vituperate their opponents during televised debates.
The angry manager started to vituperate the staff for missing the deadline.

distractors.lemma: Praise someone publicly for their achievements.
Verify the accuracy of historical documents.
Cultivate a rare species of garden flower.
Validate the claims made in a scientific report.
Venture into uncharted territories without a map.

mnemonics: Vituperate sounds like viper hate, which is what harsh, biting insults feel like.

senses.definition: Evaporating readily at normal temperatures and pressures.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Turning into a gas very easily at normal room temperatures.

examples.text: Ether is a highly volatile compound that must be stored in tightly sealed containers.
Gasoline is notoriously volatile and gives off vapors that ignite easily.
Chemistry students must handle volatile liquids inside a fume hood.
Because the solvent is so volatile, the open beaker dried out within minutes.
Volatile oils
Volatile solvents

distractors.lemma: Solidifying into a dense rock under heavy pressure.
Resistant to changes in temperature and light.
Absorbing water rapidly from the surrounding air.
Failing to dissolve in common chemical solutions.
Remaining stable in liquid form indefinitely.

senses.definition: Liable to lead to sudden change or violence.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Likely to change suddenly or become violent without warning.

examples.text: Stock markets can be extremely volatile during times of economic uncertainty.
The diplomat had to navigate a volatile political situation in the capital.
His volatile temper made everyone in the office walk on eggshells.
A volatile crowd gathered outside the courthouse as the verdict was announced.
A volatile situation with troops and rioters eager for a confrontation

distractors.lemma: Possessing a calm and predictable disposition.
Remaining stationary despite external pressure.
Showing steadfast loyalty to a single cause.
Displaying dull and uninspired emotional states.
Exhibiting profound wisdom in times of crisis.

senses.definition: Marked by erratic changeableness in affections or attachments.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Changing your mind or feelings about people very often.

examples.text: Her volatile affections meant she cycled through best friends every few weeks.
The poet was known for a volatile personality that baffled his patrons.
A volatile allegiance to different political factions ruined his career.
His volatile loyalty to various artistic movements left critics confused.
A flirt's volatile affections

distractors.lemma: Maintaining a steadfast devotion to old traditions.
Displaying a cold and unfeeling demeanor toward others.
Showing permanent dedication to a single philosophy.
Possessing a rigid mindset that resists new ideas.
Acting with consistent kindness toward strangers.

mnemonics: Volatile contains violet, and volatile liquids evaporate into thin air like vanishing ink.

senses.definition: Excessively greedy and grasping.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Having an insatiable and greedy desire for wealth or power.

examples.text: The voracious corporate raider bought out smaller companies without a second thought.
Driven by voracious ambition, the dictator seized control of all state institutions.
His voracious appetite for luxury items eventually led to financial ruin.
The land barons exhibited a voracious greed that depleted the local resources.
Paying taxes to voracious governments

distractors.lemma: Displaying a generous and giving attitude toward charity.
Content with modest possessions and simple living.
Hesitant to accept gifts from unfamiliar sources.
Showing reluctance to participate in competitions.
Marked by extreme frugality and careful spending.

senses.definition: Devouring or craving food in great quantities.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Eating huge amounts of food with great enthusiasm.

examples.text: After hiking all day, the teenagers had voracious appetites at the dinner table.
The young scholar was also a voracious reader who finished three books a week.
Our puppy has a voracious appetite and finishes his kibble in seconds.
Locusts are voracious insects that can strip a field of crops in an hour.
Voracious sharks

distractors.lemma: Showing a persistent reluctance to touch meals.
Eating very small portions due to a lack of hunger.
Preferring bland foods over seasoned dishes.
Fasting for days to achieve spiritual clarity.
Rejecting meat products in favor of water.

mnemonics: Voracious sounds like ferocious, which describes a fierce, greedy desire for more.

senses.definition: Pause or hold back in uncertainty or unwillingness.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: To hesitate or delay because you are not sure what to do.

examples.text: She did not waver when offered the promotion, accepting it immediately.
Investors tended to waver whenever market conditions became unpredictable.
He refused to waver in his commitment to the scientific method.
Do not waver now that success is finally within our grasp.

distractors.lemma: Wave a hand in greeting to passing strangers.
Weave threads together into a durable fabric.
Weep softly in moments of deep sorrow.
Wander aimlessly through the historic city streets.
Weigh heavy objects on a calibrated scale.

senses.definition: Be unsure or weak.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: To become unsteady or lack strength.

examples.text: Their resolve began to waver under the intense public scrutiny.
His confidence would occasionally waver when facing harsh criticism.
The candlelight started to waver in the sudden draft.
The athlete's stamina began to waver near the end of the marathon.

distractors.lemma: Make loud noises in a crowded marketplace.
Mix ingredients thoroughly in a large bowl.
Move quickly past obstacles on a track.
Melt metal in a high temperature furnace.
Mark boundaries clearly with wooden stakes.

senses.definition: Move hesitatingly, as if about to give way.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: To sway back and forth as if about to collapse.

examples.text: The old wooden bridge would waver dangerously under heavy loads.
The exhausted soldier started to waver before regaining his balance.
The pillar began to waver during the severe tremor.
Tall trees will waver dramatically in a fierce gale.

distractors.lemma: Walk steadily along a narrow mountain ridge.
Whisper secrets quietly to a trusted friend.
Whip cream until fluffy and stiff.
Whistle tunes while working in the garden.
Wipe surfaces clean with a damp cloth.

mnemonics: Think of waves washing back and forth, unable to decide where to settle.

senses.definition: Marked by skill in deception.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Clever at tricking people.

examples.text: The wily detective managed to outsmart the criminal syndicate.
Her wily negotiation tactics secured a very favorable contract.
The wily fox evaded the hounds by crossing the freezing river.
He relied on wily strategies to win the chess tournament.
A wily old attorney

distractors.lemma: Wild animals roaming freely across the open savanna.
Wilted flowers drooping in the afternoon sun.
Wise sages sharing ancient philosophical wisdom.
Wicked storms brewing over the dark horizon.
Worn boots showing signs of heavy use.

mnemonics: A wily person uses wiles to trick others.

senses.definition: Marked by active interest and enthusiasm.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Very excited and dedicated to a cause.

examples.text: The zealous supporters cheered loudly for their candidate.
She was zealous in her pursuit of environmental conservation.
His zealous approach to training brought remarkable athletic results.
They formed a zealous community dedicated to historic preservation.

distractors.lemma: Jealous neighbors watching from behind closed blinds.
Zealots marching through the city center in protest.
Genial hosts welcoming guests with warm smiles.
Gentle breezes rustling through the autumn leaves.
Genuine artifacts displayed behind glass museum cases.

mnemonics: Zealous people have an abundance of zeal.

senses.definition: The point above the observer that is directly opposite the nadir on the imaginary sphere against which celestial bodies appear to be projected.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: The highest point directly overhead in the sky.

examples.text: The sun reached its zenith at high noon, casting very short shadows.
The empire was at the zenith of its power during that century.
Astronomers observed stars passing directly through their zenith.
Her career reached its zenith when she won the prestigious award.

distractors.lemma: Zero tolerance policies enforced across the district.
Zealous guardians protecting the ancient temple gates.
Zestful flavors blended into a refreshing summer beverage.
Zigzag patterns painted across the concrete wall.
Zones marked clearly for restricted parking only.

mnemonics: Zenith starts with Z, the very top letter of our focus when reaching high.

senses.definition: Beguiling but harmful.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Appearing nice or harmless while actually causing damage.

examples.text: The insidious disease progressed slowly without showing any obvious symptoms.
He recognized the insidious nature of the propaganda campaign.
An insidious charm masked her true manipulative intentions.
The malware was designed to launch insidious attacks on the network.
Insidious pleasures

distractors.lemma: Inside information shared among corporate executives.
Invidious comparisons made between rival companies.
Insipid food lacking any distinct flavor or spice.
Intrepid explorers braving the harsh polar wilderness.
Invincible armies conquering vast territories abroad.

senses.definition: Intended to entrap.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Designed to trap someone in a sneaky way.

examples.text: The contract contained insidious clauses designed to trap the unwary signer.
Detectives uncovered an insidious trap set by the smuggling ring.
They laid an insidious snare along the forest trail.
The puzzle box featured an insidious mechanism that locked permanently.

distractors.lemma: Incised markings carved into the ancient stone tablet.
Incisive questions asked by the experienced journalist.
Insightful observations noted during the lecture.
Indecisive leaders unable to make a final choice.
Industrious workers completing the project ahead of schedule.

senses.definition: Working or spreading in a hidden and usually injurious way.
senses.plainLanguageDefinition: Something that causes harm slowly and secretly before you even notice.

examples.text: The insidious disease progressed quietly through her system for months without triggering any noticeable symptoms.
Cyber criminals often rely on insidious malware that hides deep within the operating system until it is too late.
Propaganda can be an insidious force that slowly alters public opinion over several generations.
They failed to notice the insidious erosion of their civil liberties until new laws restricted their daily freedom.
Glaucoma is an insidious disease

distractors.lemma: Existing within the physical boundaries of a specific region.
Pertaining to the careful study of ancient coins and medals.
Marked by loud and boisterous celebration during public events.
Characterized by sudden and violent outbursts of physical energy.
Relating to the intricate design of decorative interior woodwork.

mnemonics: Inside, an insidious plot hides its harm.
